items: A regex describes a **set of strings**; `java.util.regex` provides `Pattern` and `Matcher`.
**`matches()` tests the whole string; `find()` searches inside it.** This is the distinction to remember.
`[abc]` is a character class, `[a-z]` a range, `[^abc]` a negation, `.` any character.
Repetition: `*` zero or more, `+` one or more, `?` zero or one, `{x}`, `{x,y}`, `{x,}`.
Shorthands `\d \w \s` need **double backslashes** in Java string literals.
`split()` and `replaceAll()` take **regexes**, so metacharacters must be escaped.
